body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 1a7a1cefeecc76da38b2ed125619e21629fd4a69 -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blocking finding. The change does what #3608 asks: the window asks, and a script or an agent is refused by name, before a save writes over the project's own file that changed on disk. I reviewed a draft on the maintainer's order. I did not flag it ready, did not merge, and did not change its draft state.

**What looks good**
- The check runs before `project::save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:54-55`, and `crates/ui/src/state.rs:4738` in `save_project_path`). The refusal and the prompt both come before the temp file, the write probe and the rename. No path truncates or writes before the answer.
- Every desktop open stamps the file: the File > Open dialog, the Recent list, `launch_file` and drag-drop all go through `open_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4676`). Every headless save goes through `v_save`, and `v_load` stamps on open. No save path bypasses the guard.
- The stamp is taken after `project::save` returns `Ok`, so our own next save does not ask. The write probe of `project::save` opens the old file without writing and runs before the rename, so it does not move the new stamp. The tests pin both.
- The quit path is safe. When Quit -> Save is held because the file changed, the history stays dirty and `resolve_unsaved` keeps the document open (`crates/ui/src/unsaved.rs:81-95`). The test pins this.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code. The new files are 44-93 lines. No file grows past 400 by a meaningful amount; the files already over 400 grow by a few lines.
- No `Cargo.toml`, `.cargo/`, `build.rs`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `xtask/` or `PROCESS_VERSION` change, and no new crate dependency. `Changelog:` and `Fixes #3608` are present. `cam.d.ts`, the MCP tool schema, `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the two guide pages agree with the new argument.

**Results, merged with `origin/main` `79cf28630`**
Trial merge was clean, no conflicts. Built and tested locally on Linux, not on the runner: the fork author has read-only access, and this review was told not to start `pr-test.yml`.
- Build: `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run`, exit 0.
- app `save_overwrite_guard` (the 7 new pins): 7 passed, 0 failed.
- app `project_roundtrip`: 82 passed, 0 failed (holds the #3510 temp-file/rename pins, e.g. `a_failed_project_save_keeps_the_old_file`).
- app `machine_edit`: 13 passed, 0 failed.
- app `mcp_live`: 14 passed, 0 failed.
- app `mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed, 0 failed.
- app `scripting`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 1498 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored (the 6 `save_guard_tests` and `layout_window_overwrite_prompt` among them).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, exit 0. The only warning is the pre-existing `unused workspace dependency truck-polymesh` manifest note, which is not from this diff.

**Targeted tests (heavy lanes at review)**
- No post or toolpath change, so the example catalog suites do not apply.
- Light lane: 2 `camcraft-motion` twins (the fixed guard set), both green in release: `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` and `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light`.
- The `P1` here is data loss, not a wrong output under the safety floor (no G-code, collision check, simulation or geometry), so no targeted heavy step applies (#3556). `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` reaches the app heavy targets only because `crates/app/src` changed; I did not run them, and no PR is owed them (#3556).

**Findings: none blocking.**

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- Known limit, already in the decision and the PR body: the guard compares size and modification time (`crates/app/src/project/disk_stamp.rs:57-61`). A same-size rewrite inside one modification-time tick is not seen. Concrete case: an SMB share that keeps the time in steps of 1-2 s, and a colleague's save of a same-size project within the same step. That is the issue's own "sync client / shared folder" case. The issue asked for a size-and-time stamp, and a content digest was weighed and dropped for cost, so this is the accepted design. I record it here so the maintainer sees it, not as a defect.
- The bridge that keeps an agent's new stamp in the window (`crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs:65-66`, three lines) is not driven by a test. The app test pins the live seam's `doc_stamp` round-trip; a regression in this filter would cause an unnecessary prompt, not data loss. A small UI test would close it.
- After a held-save quit, if the user picks Overwrite, the save writes but the quit does not re-run; the user quits again. This is documented as intended (`crates/ui/src/save_guard.rs:75-93`, decision "Considered and dropped"). It is safe, only a second action.
- I built and tested on Linux. The diff adds no `cfg(windows)` or per-OS pinned value, so no Windows-only reading is owed. The browser/wasm build and a real second process or network share are not driven here, as the PR body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
